business_problem: RMIT needed secure, high-performance cloud research environments that could handle large simulations, geospatial knowledge graphs, and AI workloads much faster than on-premises servers while making advanced infrastructure accessible to researchers.
solution_summary: RMIT built its RACE research-computing ecosystem on AWS to give researchers secure, well-architected environments for HPC, data science, and emerging compute-intensive workloads. Amazon EC2 and AWS ParallelCluster provide the elastic compute backbone for simulation-heavy research, while Amazon SageMaker and Amazon SageMaker Studio support data-science and AI workflows, and Amazon Braket expands access to advanced experimentation. RACE packages these services with training, consultancy, and secure environment templates so researchers can test ideas quickly without building their own infrastructure from scratch. The result is a reusable cloud research platform that cuts solve times from months to days, enables very large aerospace and geospatial analyses, and improves funding leverage by giving more than 550 researchers access to on-demand high-performance computing.

data_flow: Research datasets and simulation jobs are provisioned through RACE into AWS ParallelCluster and Amazon EC2 environments, with downstream AI and analytics work supported in Amazon SageMaker and SageMaker Studio and broader experimentation enabled through Amazon Braket.
business_outcome: RMIT onboarded more than 550 researchers, achieved up to 100x performance improvement for some workloads, cut aerospace solving time from nearly 3 months to 3.5 days, and processed more than 2 million interlinked geospatial records in under an hour.
